test_accuracy_modular_addition.comparison: candidate is 82% worse than baseline (0.082 vs 0.453)

gradient_health_mean_norm.comparison: candidate gradient norms slightly higher but both healthy

param_efficiency_params_per_accuracy_poi.comparison: candidate has fewer params per accuracy point (589 params total) but only because accuracy is so low the ratio is misleading

reaches_99pct_test_accuracy_with_less_co.detail: Test accuracy reached only 8.17% (best: 8.59%). Nowhere near 99%.

maintains_performance_across_all_primes.detail: Per-prime accuracy ranges from 5.6% (p=31) to 46.2% (p=5). Performance collapses for larger primes, indicating memorization of small-prime examples rather than learning modular structure.

higher_test_accuracy_per_flop.detail: Candidate achieved 8.17% vs baseline 45.3%. Candidate is strictly worse at every compute level.

gradient_norms_exceed_50_for_3_consecuti.detail: Max gradient norm was 0.216. Gradients stayed well below 50 throughout.

test_accuracy_below_60pct_at_50pct_budge.detail: At epoch 5000 (50% of 10000 budget), test accuracy was 6.92%. This is below 60% and triggers the failure criterion.

loss_above_initial_at_20pct_budget.detail: Initial train loss 3.381, at epoch 2000 (20% budget) train loss was 2.517. Loss did decrease below initial value.

training_dynamics.detail: Model plateaued at ~17% train accuracy and ~8% test accuracy within the first 200 epochs and showed no improvement over the remaining 9800 epochs. No grokking, no delayed generalization, no phase transition observed.

rejection_reasons: Test accuracy 8.17% is 82% below baseline (45.3%) — the architecture cannot learn modular addition
Failure criterion triggered: test accuracy 6.92% at 50% compute budget, far below the 60% threshold
No success criteria met — not even partial progress toward any criterion
Training plateaued within first 200 epochs with no recovery over remaining 9800 epochs
Per-prime analysis shows near-random performance for all primes >= 11, indicating the 589-param model memorized a few small-prime examples rather than learning algebraic structure
Initial gradient norms were very small (0.093), and LR was capped at 1.0, suggesting the Cayley algebra compositor architecture produces weak gradient signals that prevent meaningful learning
